title: Flood Preparedness and Safety
summary: Protective actions before, during, and after flood incidents, electrical safety, and contamination hazards.
content:
1. MONITOR WARNINGS: Call Floodline (0345 988 1188) or check the Environment Agency service if internet is available. Follow advice from emergency services immediately.

2. SECURE UTILITIES AND PROPERTY:
- If floodwater is imminent and it is safe to do so, switch off electricity at the mains consumer unit and turn off the gas supply and main water stopcock.
- NEVER touch electrical switches, plugs, or circuit boxes while standing in water or if equipment is wet.
- Move essential valuables, medication, warm clothing, electronics, and documents upstairs or to high shelving.

3. PROTECT YOURSELF INDOORS:
- If trapped inside a building, move upstairs or to high ground with essentials and charged phones.
- Do not enter enclosed attics unless an exit to the roof exists, to prevent getting trapped by rising water.

4. AVOID FLOODWATER OUTDOORS:
- NEVER walk, swim, or drive through floodwater.
- Just 15 cm (6 inches) of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet.
- Just 30 cm (12 inches) of moving water will float most passenger cars.
- Hidden dangers include open manhole covers, submerged debris, and electrical currents.

5. CONTAMINATION AND HYGIENE:
- Floodwater commonly contains raw sewage, harmful chemicals, and bacteria.
- Avoid skin contact. If exposed, wash hands and skin with clean water and soap immediately.
- Discard any food, drinks, or medications that have come into contact with floodwater.
